description: Committee recommends 1st Avenue BRT changes: with-flow lanes, 4 stations.

segments.title: BRT Project Overview and Rationale
description: Project began almost 10 years ago, guided by 2016 Growth Plan.
Growth Plan aimed for complete communities and robust transportation.
Rapid transit facilities needed as demand grows for ridership.
City needs to provide choices beyond car-centric growth.

chips.text: 2016 Growth Plan provided roadmap for city's development
If nothing changes, city will be forcing people to take a car

segments.title: First Avenue BRT Conceptual Design Revisions
description: Road safety audit identified conflicts with bus operations and pedestrians.
Design options considered parking retention and one-way street conversion.
Preferred option balances parking, pedestrian space, and traffic flow.
Changes include with-flow lanes, more stations, and parking reduction.

chips.text: Multimodal level of service considered all users, not just vehicles
Businesses and property owners along First Avenue

segments.title: Snow Removal Plan for First Avenue BRT
description: Current snow removal costs $90,000 annually for First Avenue.
Proposed plan estimates $255,000 annually for First Avenue.
Work will be done at night by private contractors when buses are offline.
Consideration for contractor to clear sidewalks to save cleanup.

chips.text: $255,000 per year estimated for snow grading and removal
Planning on multi-year contract for private contractors
Adjacent property and business owners for sidewalk clearing

segments.title: Midtown Plaza Supports BRT Changes
description: Midtown Plaza fully supports the rapid bus route on First Avenue.
BRT will improve accessibility, foot traffic, and downtown vibrancy.
Acknowledges temporary construction challenges, stresses long-term benefits.
Believes off-street parking is sufficient to offset losses.

chips.text: Midtown Plaza fully supports rapid bus route on First Avenue
Midtown Plaza, its 4.3 million annual visitors, and employees

segments.title: NSBA Raises Concerns on BRT Changes
description: NSBA supported 2019 plan, but not current proposal due to changes.
Concerns include 61 parking spots lost and increased travel times.
Reduction to one lane raises questions about long-term functionality.
Major concerns about winter operations and safety plans.

chips.text: NSBA raises significant concerns about proposed BRT changes

segments.title: Downtown BID Expresses Business Concerns
description: Downtown BID supports better transit but design must be thoughtful.
Concerns about restricted left turns and limited alley access for businesses.
Questions the removal of 61 parking spots downtown.
Consultation felt like information sharing, not input gathering.

chips.text: Downtown BID expresses substantial concerns from businesses and property owners
Over a thousand businesses, 3,000 residents, 18,000 employees downtown
Survey for 2nd Avenue median decision had only 10 respondents
We cannot jeopardize businesses that sustain downtown today

segments.title: Sherry Terraceoff Highlights Discrepancies in BRT Plan
description: Highlights significant changes from 2019 approved plan.
Questions traffic modeling assumptions and future growth impacts.
Compares First Avenue to Preston Avenue, finding it misleading.
Calls for robust operational plan including snow clearing and detours.

segments.title: Bus Riders of Saskatoon Supports BRT Recommendations
description: Bus Riders of Saskatoon urges committee to endorse administration's recommendations.

description: Raises concerns about snow removal during BRT operation and platform design.
